title: Worth a third of the Qur'an
hookLine: the Prophet ﷺ said this short surah equals a third of the Qur'an (Bukhari)

lines: SMALL THINGS THAT WEIGH A LOT.
A THIRD OF THE WHOLE BOOK?
cards: Some things weigh more than their size. A wedding ring. A two-line text that says we need to talk.
A child's drawing on the fridge. Yesterday's surah had four lines.

Today, a strange claim about it, made by the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ himself and recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari: those four lines weigh as much as a third of the whole Qur'an. The whole book, and these four lines are a third?

teach.b: A companion heard a man reciting qul huwa Allahu ahad at night, over and over. In the morning he told the Prophet, a little as if the man were cutting corners.

teach.h: IT EQUALS A THIRD OF THE QUR'AN.
teach.b: The Prophet answered: by the One in whose hand my soul is, it equals a third of the Qur'an. Another report in Bukhari has him asking his companions: can any of you recite a third of the Qur'an in a night?
Who could manage that, they said. And he told them: this surah is a third. What does it mean?
One well-known answer from the scholars: the Qur'an speaks of three great things.

teach.h: WHO GOD IS, WHAT GOD ASKS, WHAT HAPPENS.
teach.b: Who Allah is; what He commands, the law; and what happens, the stories and the promise of what's coming. Al-Ikhlas is the first of those, pure and whole.
Scholars add a caution: it equals a third in reward and meaning, not as a substitute. Reciting it three times doesn't mean you've read the whole book. One more story.

A man leading his companions in prayer ended every recitation with this surah. They told the Prophet, who said: ask him why. The man said: because it describes the Most Merciful, and I love to recite it.
And the Prophet said: tell him that Allah loves him.
Short, and heavy. The weight isn't in the length. It's in what the words hold, and in the love of the one reciting them.

how: Many Muslims recite al-Ikhlas often, in the prayers, at night and before sleep, and some recite it three times in memory of the hadith that it equals a third of the Qur'an.

who Allah is, what He commands, what happens. al-Ikhlas is the first, whole.

games.q: a prayer leader ends every recitation with al-Ikhlas, and his companions tell the Prophet. what does the Prophet say?
games.why: ask him why. the man said he loved it because it describes the Most Merciful, and the Prophet said: tell him that Allah loves him.

practice: If you pray, you can recite al-Ikhlas slowly in one of today's prayers, or right now, one line per breath, letting each line land before the next.
If you don't, pick one short line you love from anywhere and say it as slowly as you've ever said anything. There's a lot of room inside something small when you don't rush it.
